#### 1. microcephaly 6, primary, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.805)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:17272)

**Proposed mechanism:** CPAP (HGNC:17272) —DISRUPTS→ cytosol (GO:0005829); cytosol (GO:0005829) —LEADS_TO→ cytoplasmic microtubule organization (GO:0034370); cytoplasmic microtubule organization (GO:0034370) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); cytoplasmic microtubule organization (GO:0034370) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001248). Loss-of-function mutations in CPAP disrupt its function within the cytosol, leading to impaired cytoplasmic microtubule organization. This disorganization underlies the microcephaly and global developmental delay observed in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in CPAP associated with either disease that exhibit gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if CPAP variants are found at a high frequency (>1%) in control populations (e.g., gnomAD) and lack segregation with disease, this would also weaken the hypothesis. _(variant: HGNC:17272)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CPAP in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies that aim to restore normal microtubule organization or function, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
